primary_diagnosis_source.text:
ADMISSION DIAGNOSIS:
Right tibial plateau fracture.

secondary_diagnoses: medial meniscus tear on the right side
procedures_performed: Open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) of right Schatzker III tibial plateau fracture with partial medial meniscectomy.

diagnosis_explanation:
You have a broken bone in your lower leg. This is your right shin bone. It is near your knee joint. You also tore a piece of cartilage. This is on the inside of your right knee.

You have a thyroid problem. Your thyroid gland is in your neck. It helps your body use energy. You also have diabetes. This means your body has trouble using sugar for energy. Bronchitis means your airways are swollen. Congestive heart failure means your heart does not pump blood as well as it should.
medication_rationale:
Lasix 80 mg:
This medicine helps your body get rid of extra fluid.
It can help reduce swelling from your injury.
You may urinate more often. This is normal.
Call your doctor if you feel very dizzy.
Also call if you get muscle cramps.
Call right away if your heart beats very fast.

Lovenox 30 mg:
This medicine helps prevent blood clots.
It is given because you are not moving your leg much.
You may notice some bruising or bleeding at the injection spot.
Call your doctor if you have severe headaches or nosebleeds.
Also call if you notice blood in your urine or stool.

Vicodin 5/500 mg:
This medicine helps control pain from your injury.
It is a pain reliever.
You may feel sleepy or dizzy.
You may also get a dry mouth or feel constipated.
Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing or feel very confused.

Combivent nebulizer:
This medicine helps you breathe more easily.
It relaxes the muscles in your airways.
You may feel your heart beat faster.
You might also feel shaky or get a headache.
Call your doctor if your breathing gets worse.

Zithromax 250 mg:
This medicine helps fight any infections.
You were given this medicine to help prevent infection.
You may get an upset stomach or diarrhea.
Call your doctor if you get a severe rash or hives.
Also call if you have watery or bloody stools.

Guaifenesin Long-Acting:
This medicine helps thin mucus in your airways.
It can make it easier to cough up mucus.
You may get a headache or feel dizzy.
Call your doctor if you get a rash.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You will likely feel tired and have some pain.
- Keep your right leg still. Do not put any weight on it.
- Use your CPM machine as directed when in bed.
- Wear your anti-swelling stockings on your legs.
- Eat your regular diet.
- Call your doctor if you have sudden chest pain or trouble breathing.
- Your goal this week is to rest and follow all instructions.

**Week 2:**
- Pain may start to lessen. You might still feel quite tired.
- Keep your right leg nonweightbearing.
- Continue using the CPM machine and wearing your stockings.
- Eat your regular diet.
- Call your doctor if you see new swelling or redness in your leg.
- Your goal this week is to get comfortable with resting and moving in bed.

**Week 3:**
- You may start to feel a little more energy.
- You still cannot put weight on your right leg.
- Keep using the CPM machine and wearing your stockings.
- Eat your regular diet.
- Call your doctor if you have a fever over 101 degrees Fahrenheit.
- Your goal this week is to manage your pain with rest and medicine.

**Week 4:**
- You might feel a bit more comfortable. Fatigue may decrease.
- Continue to keep all weight off your right leg.
- Keep wearing your anti-swelling stockings.
- Eat your regular diet.
- Call your doctor if you notice any clear fluid or pus from your incision.
- Your goal this week is to do gentle leg exercises as shown by your doctor.

**When to expect improvement:**
- You will likely feel gradual improvement over many weeks.
- Continue to follow all weightbearing and activity limits.
- Keep up with wearing your anti-swelling stockings.
- Healing takes time and patience.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- You cannot breathe: Your body needs oxygen right now.
- Chest pain that will not stop: Your heart needs help now.
- Face drooping or arm weakness: These are stroke signs. Minutes matter.
- Uncontrolled bleeding that will not stop: Call 911 for help.
- You lose consciousness or faint: Call 911 right away.
- Seizure happens: Call 911 and stay with them.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Fever over 101 degrees F: You may have an infection.
- Wound looks red and angry: Streaks mean infection is spreading.
- Pain is severe and not helped: Get help for bad pain.
- Leg swells badly with pain: This could be a blood clot.
- Cannot keep any fluids down: You need help to stay hydrated.
- Confusion or disorientation starts: This sign needs medical review.
- You fall and get hurt: Get checked for a new injury.
- Weight gain of 2+ lbs daily: Fluid may be building up.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Mild pain that is slowly better: This is normal healing.
- Wound healing slower than expected: Watch for any new signs.
- Mild swelling without pain: This can happen while you heal.
- Nausea without vomiting: Try sipping small amounts of fluid.
- Fatigue that is slowly better: Rest and take it easy.
- Questions about your medicine: Your doctor can explain doses.
